appliesTo: any person who discloses, or threatens to disclose, explicit synthetic media of an identifiable person

exposure.penaltyUnit: per felony offense (fine; plus up to 10 years imprisonment)

sources.prohibition: § 2, 18-6606(1)(a) — 'Discloses explicit synthetic media and knows or reasonably should know that: (i) An identifiable person portrayed in whole or in part in the explicit synthetic media did not consent to such disclosure'
sources.coveredSubjects: § 2, 18-6606(4)(c) — '"Identifiable individual" means a person who is portrayed in whole or in part in synthetic media and who is recognizable by the person's face, likeness, or other distinguishing characteristic'
sources.penaltyMax: § 2, 18-6606(3) — 'a felony punishable by imprisonment for a period no more than ten (10) years, or by a fine of no more than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000), or by both such fine and imprisonment'
sources.penaltyUnit: § 2, 18-6606(2)–(3) — 'A person who violates subsection (1) of this section is guilty of a misdemeanor unless such person is guilty of a felony as provided in subsection (3)'

flags: Base offense is a misdemeanor with no fine amount stated (18-6606(2)); coded penaltyMax is the felony tier, which applies only when the identifiable person is under 18 or the offender has a prior violation within 5 years (18-6606(3))
Section 1 also amends the separate video voyeurism offense (18-6605, real-imagery NCII), extending it to threats or conspiracy to disseminate, publish or sell — outside the ai-crimes param vocabulary

Safe harbor for interactive computer services, information services, and telecommunication services for content provided by another person unless the provider intentionally aids or abets (18-6606(6)); no company compliance duty imposed
Extortion variant included: possessing and threatening to disclose with intent to obtain money or other valuable consideration (18-6606(1)(c))
